transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I keep going back over my jobs again and again. I'm an electrician, and... I just can't seem to stop checking my work. 

I'll check the breakers, the labels, the torque marks on the screws... I even take photos of everything before I leave so I can look at them later. And sometimes even that's not enough, and I'll actually drive all the way back to a job site just to make absolutely sure I did it right. It's getting to the point where a really simple install is taking me way longer than it ever should, and the other guys are starting to notice. I just need to figure out how to get a handle on it.
When you're checking your work over and over, do you feel like these checks are really necessary, or do you recognize that you might be overdoing it?

I definitely know I'm overdoing it. Like I was just saying with the breakers and the photos... I know a simple install shouldn't take me this long. I've been doing this for years, so deep down, I know the work is fine. 

But it's like I just have to go back over the jobs again and again, or even drive all the way back to the site, just to convince my brain it's actually done right. I realize it's not really necessary, especially since the other guys are starting to notice how much time I'm wasting, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it.

You mentioned knowing deep down that your work is fine and that you're overdoing the checking. But in those moments when you feel the urge to check or drive back to a job site, do you actually believe something might be wrong, or do you recognize it's irrational even as you're doing it?

I know it's irrational, even while it's happening. But it's like... even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I start thinking that maybe I missed one loose neutral, or that I left something that could start a fire. 

I try to shake it off, and I tell myself I'm being ridiculous because I've done this a thousand times. But the thought just follows me all the way home. So I guess my logical brain knows the work is fine, but that fear just won't let up until I go back and look at it one more time.

latest_inference.note: Patient demonstrates clear insight into the irrationality of compulsions (checking work repeatedly, driving back to job sites, taking photos) while being unable to resist them. The intrusive thoughts about potential danger (loose neutral, fire hazard) are recognized as excessive. This is classic OCD with good insight. F42.2 (OCD with poor/absent insight) is ruled out because patient explicitly states 'I know it's irrational, even while it's happening' and recognizes the checking is unnecessary.
